name: adx_strong_trend_pullback
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when institutional TWAP algorithms execute large directional mandates, the index forms persistent 2-4 minute micro-trends reflected in ADX(36) rising above 25. Retail momentum chasers and short-term scalpers periodically take profit, pulling NIFTY 8-15 spot points back to the 2-minute EMA — the lowest bar of the pullback touches the EMA while the close stays near it. These shallow retracements are immediately absorbed by the institutional order flow still partially unfilled: the moment NIFTY's 5-second close reclaims above the 2-min EMA (+DI > -DI confirming buy-side dominance), the next wave of institutional program buys resumes, creating a 10-20 spot point continuation within 30-90 seconds. The EMA touch-and-reclaim specifically filters for entries where selling pressure exhausted at the EMA support rather than cutting through it, maximising directional probability.

indicators.name: adx_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute ADX is the TRADE TRIGGER for this strategy — we hold 30-90 seconds so the trend context should be 2-3× the hold horizon. ADX(36)=3 min is long enough to confirm a genuine directional regime (not a 30-second spike) yet short enough to detect nascent institutional micro-trends early, before they extend too far for pullback entries. Original used ADX(14) on 1-min = 14-minute trend measurement; compressing to 3 min because we're entering pullbacks within micro-trends, not macro daily trends.

indicators.name: plus_di_36
indicators.purpose: Directional indicator confirming buy-side (+DI > -DI) or sell-side dominance (-DI > +DI). Same period as ADX for consistency; measures which direction the institutional program is running.

indicators.name: minus_di_36
indicators.purpose: Paired with +DI(36). When -DI > +DI, institutional selling pressure exceeds buying — enter PE on EMA pullback bounce.

indicators.name: ema_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute EMA (24 bars × 5s) is the pullback target level. On 1-min bars, the original used EMA(20) = 20-minute smoothing — far too slow for our 30-90 second hold horizon. The 2-min EMA acts as dynamic support/resistance during NIFTY micro-trends: shallow retracements stop exactly at this level before continuation. If we used a longer EMA (e.g., EMA(60)=5 min), price would need to fall much further, missing the optimal pullback entry. Shorter than EMA(12)=1 min to avoid noise from individual 5-second wicks.

conditions: low[i] <= ema_24[i] (price touched 2-min EMA from above — pullback reached the level)
close[i] > ema_24[i] (close recovered above EMA — selling absorbed, trend resuming)
buy_ce.confirmation: All four conditions on same 5-second bar. The low-touches-but-close-above pattern is the core signal: it confirms the EMA acted as support rather than being broken.

conditions: high[i] >= ema_24[i] (price touched 2-min EMA from below — bounce reached the resistance level)
close[i] < ema_24[i] (close rejected below EMA — buying absorbed, downtrend resuming)
buy_pe.confirmation: All four conditions on same 5-second bar. High-touches-but-close-below confirms EMA acted as resistance.

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts = ~6 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. In a genuine micro-trend pullback, if NIFTY retreats 6+ spot points below the EMA close (after having reclaimed it), the EMA support has failed and the trend thesis is broken — this defines the maximum tolerable adverse move within the 30-90s hold window. Typical 30-second adverse moves on failed entries are 4-8 spot pts; 6 spot pts (3 option pts) stops out ~80% of losers before they extend further.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts = ~10 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. Successful EMA pullback entries in strong NIFTY micro-trends (ADX>25) see 10-20 spot point continuation in the next 30-90 seconds as the institutional order flow resumes; 5 pts captures the first 50-75% of the expected move at a 1:1.67 R:R. Consistent with typical NIFTY 1-minute moves (3-7 pts) and targeting the lower half given the short 30-90s hold window.

filters.vix_filter: none — micro-trend pullback works in both high and low VIX regimes; ADX itself filters out choppy conditions
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST (09:30 start allows ADX(36) 72-bar warmup = 6 min; avoid last 10 min slippage)
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is a noisy secondary signal at 5s resolution
filters.trend_filter: ADX(36) > 25 is the primary trend filter
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — ADX pullback patterns may erode as more intraday algos learn the same level; differentiated by using 5s resolution to catch the EMA touch faster than 1-min competitors

adaptation_notes: Original: ADX(14) on 1-min NIFTY100 stocks, EMA(20) on 1-min (= 20-min smoothing), hold 40-100 min, ATR-based stops (20-40 pts). Converted: ADX(36) on 5s NIFTY index (= 3-min trend, 4.7× shorter to match 30-90s hold vs 40-100 min), EMA(24) on 5s (= 2-min, 10× shorter because pullback entry needs near-term support not multi-hour moving average), stops in option premium pts not ATR. The pullback mechanic (low touches EMA, close above) is preserved exactly from the original — it's the most valuable part of the strategy. ADX filter is the regime qualifier that eliminates choppy days. Key differentiation from adx_trend_strength_v1 (already converted): that strategy uses ADX(60) + VWAP alignment to enter ANYWHERE in the trend; this strategy specifically waits for the EMA pullback-and-reclaim, producing a tighter entry timing and different signal distribution.
weaknesses: ADX(36) at 5s lags by ~3 minutes — a trend that reverses 2 minutes in may still show ADX>25 at entry
EMA touch-and-reclaim at 5s resolution can trigger on intrabar wicks rather than genuine pullbacks on choppy days
During low-volatility compressed sessions, EMA pullbacks are too shallow (1-2 pts) and don't produce enough continuation for 5pt targets
NIFTY micro-trends cluster around economic data releases — without event filter, may trade through high-slippage news bars
